title: bookmarks --count silently stops at 50: follow X's cursor
description:
Found while closing bendx-jyu, live on 2026-10-12.

`bookmarks --count 200 --json` returns 50 tweets, exit 0, no note. X's bookmark
timeline takes `count` as a PAGE SIZE (ceiling 50), and the response carries a
bottom cursor that bird never follows:

  data.data.bookmark_timeline_v2.timeline.instructions[0].entries[]
    ... last two entries are content.entryType == TimelineTimelineCursor,
        cursorType "Bottom" (and "Top"), with .value as the next-page token

Probe (same tree as commit ed01528, bird's own request vector from --dry-run,
`cursor` added to variables): page 1 status 200 / 50 tweets / cursor HBaW8/eR0e6X..;
page 2 with that cursor status 200 / 50 tweets / 0 overlap / a fresh bottom
cursor. So the cue works and the loop is possible.

Why it matters: chiebukuro's bookmarks stream is its only X input and asks for
`-n N`. Above 50 it silently ingests the same first page every run, so nothing
new ever lands and the shortfall is invisible.

Deliverable: `bookmarks --count N` follows the bottom cursor until N tweets
arrive, X stops offering a cursor, or a page guard trips; the folded
`data.tweets[]` accumulates the pages in X's order; `--raw` keeps the last page
as X sent it. Offline suite + e2e coverage for the two-page case, and the guides
say what --count means.

Acceptance: on the probe account `bookmarks --count 200 --json` answers 200
tweets (live recorded, cursor pages 1..4) and `--count 50` makes one request;
e2e proves the second request carries the cursor from the first; PROOF, the
eight offline suites, and tests/e2e.sh are green.

Verified rather than assumed (clean worktree at 39e60f1 printed SOME PROOFS FAIL), repaired the designed way (reopen -> commit the missing file -> re-run -> re-gate at the new sha -> re-close), and the stale receipts carry a SUPERSEDED header saying exactly why instead of being deleted; deviations: (1) the bead's premise was wrong -- X does not cap a bookmarks page at 50, bird clamped --count to 1..50 silently and X answers up to the count it is given, capping a page near a hundred (measured 97..100 for asks of 100 and 200), recorded as a bead comment; (2) because a page can carry ~99 past the ask, the fold cuts the joined pages to exactly --count; (3) --count above a verb's ceiling is now REFUSED (exit 2) instead of silently rounded down, which changed one existing e2e case ("a search count is clamped to fifty" became "a count past a verb's ceiling is refused") and the guides with it; (4) search and mentions still read one page -- they have cursors too, but nothing asked for them and this bead is the bookmarks stream; PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — the truncation was two causes, a silent clamp and an unread cursor, both fixed where every caller routes through them; prove-it-works — the live probe corrected the bead's premise and the trim exists because the measurement, not the design, said a page overshoots; sequence-verifiable-units — the missing file was caught by proving the committed tree rather than the working one, and the repair path is the ledger's own reopen/gate/close rather than a forced row.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
Premise corrected by the live probe while working this (2026-10-12).

The bead said "X caps a bookmarks page at 50". That was wrong, and the 50 came from bird's own policy: Cfg.read_count clamped --count to 1..50 and did it silently, so `--count 200` never reached X as 200. Measured directly, with bird's own request vector from --dry-run plus a cursor added by hand: ask 60 -> page 1 = 60; ask 100 -> page 1 = 97, page 2 with the cursor = 99, no overlap; ask 200 -> page 1 = 97, page 2 = 99, page 3 = 100.

So X answers up to the count it is given and caps a page near a hundred. Two consequences for the fix: the total arrives in a couple of pages rather than four, and the page that meets the ask can carry about 99 more than was wanted, which is why the fold cuts the joined pages to exactly --count. The clamp is now a refusal naming the range (1..50 search/mentions, 1..500 bookmarks).

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
REPAIR, found right after the first close: PROOF.bend was left out of commit 39e60f1. The work commit therefore does not prove -- `bend PROOF.bend` in a clean worktree at that sha fails with "a src/domain.VerbBookmarks pattern with 2 fields", which is exactly the pattern the commit grew -- so the unit-test-verified receipt claimed a fence pass at a tree that does not pass it, and the binding was false, not merely stale.

Verified before repairing, not assumed: `git worktree add /tmp/bendx-sha 39e60f1` then `bend PROOF.bend` inside it prints SOME PROOFS FAIL. The fix is the designed remedy: reopen, commit the missing file, re-run the fence at the new sha, re-gate both rows there, and re-close citing the new sha. The stale receipts are annotated rather than deleted; the live evidence is re-run at the new sha because "live at this sha" has to mean this sha.

title: Login: import the browser session and X's rotating settings into one cache
description: Why: the values X rotates (web bearer, four operation ids) and the two session cookies arrive from two unrelated places, and doing that by hand is a script that rots. Scope: a 'login' verb that reads the session out of Chrome (keychain key -> PBKDF2-SHA1 -> AES-128-CBC, v10) or Firefox (one sqlite3 select), fetches X's client bundle for the bearer and the operation ids, writes one settings cache (keys are flag names, mode 0600) that every later run reads with no credential flags; --settings-path, --cookie-source, --cookie-db, --chrome-key, --web-home, --bundle-base; src/scan.bend, src/cookies.bend, src/bundle.bend; a login guide, README/CHANGELOG/ADR sections; install.sh to compile and install the CLI. Acceptance: the four login refusals fire before anything runs; a wrongly-decrypted cookie is a refusal naming --chrome-key, never a cache written with it; a run with no credentials uses the cache; login with no --settings-path works on a machine where ~/.config/bird does not exist; the e2e login case asserts what the stand-in server received, not how many requests it got.
close_reason: Login lands end to end: the browser's session, X's rotating settings, one 0600 settings cache, eleven new e2e cases and the new suites; two defects the tests could not see were found by running the installed binary by hand (the missing settings directory, and a request-count assertion standing in for a property). Landed as one commit because the login feature and its installer share one fence and the overlapping docs cannot be split without interactive staging; the installer is named in that commit. Coordination was open in the captain pane (dispatcher absent, no live fleet, zero ready beads at briefing time): no fleet tooling was live, so no reservations beyond the local toron ones and no mail were sent. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — every gate above was run, not described; fix-root-causes — the missing directory is made at the write rather than handled per caller, and the e2e assertion now checks the property instead of the tally.

title: A write that timed out is reported retryable, which invites a duplicate post
description:
Found by reviewing the transport against the effect-oriented laws (unknown outcome must stay unknown; a retry may only wrap idempotent work).

The mechanism. View.envelope derives the boolean from the code alone -- J.of_bool(D.ErrCode.retryable(code)) -- and Http.transport_failed maps every curl status except 26 and 37 to ErrNetwork, which is retryable. curl 28 (timed out), 52 (empty reply) and 56 (failed while receiving) all mean the request WAS sent and the answer was lost, so for bird tweet and bird reply the CreateTweet POST may already have landed. The run answers {"id":"network","retryable":true} with the hint "curl exit 28".

Why it matters. tweet and reply are the only two non-idempotent verbs in the program. docs/guides/agents.mdx:51 states the contract as "error.retryable is true for exactly rate_limited, network and upstream, so a caller that wants to back off and retry reads one boolean", README.md:199 repeats it and docs/guides/reading.mdx:208 restates it. An agent that obeys the documented contract re-posts a tweet that already exists. Nothing in the envelope, the hint or the notes says the outcome is unknown.

The contrast that shows the gap. The missing-attachment case got exactly this treatment (http.bend 210-219, ADR 0001 section 8, gotcha 2): 26/37 were mapped to usage with retryable false because "a path that does not exist will not exist on the next attempt". The reasoning is right and was never applied to the other half -- a request that was sent and not answered is not safe to repeat either, and unlike a missing file it may have succeeded.

The decision this needs (this is why the bead is not fixed in place). retryable is currently a pure function of the code, and the code table is frozen API (err.id, the ADR section 8 table, agents.mdx). Either (a) keep id: network for these on a read and make the write case a distinct outcome the envelope can name, amending the one-sentence contract, or (b) add a code for an indeterminate outcome, which changes ErrCode.all() and therefore the published schema. Whichever is chosen, curl 6 and 7 (could not resolve, could not connect) must stay retryable for a write too: nothing was sent.

Acceptance: a unit case pins that a write whose curl status is 28, 52 or 56 answers retryable false with a hint that says the request was sent and the outcome is unknown; the same statuses on a read stay retryable; a write's 6/7 stays retryable. e2e exercises one of them against the stand-in. The ADR, agents.mdx and README stop claiming retryable is exactly the three codes.

title: A page token that did not move ends the walk; the paged stand-in answers the request
description:
Two holes left by the bookmark pagination, both of which the suite could not see.

1. src/update.bend: Update.page_more stopped on three facts (the ask was met, X offered no token, the page carried nothing). A page that hands back the token it was fetched with passes all three, so the walk re-read that page and added the same tweets again, once per page, until --count was met: under --count 500 that is up to 500 identical requests and an answer holding the same tweets many times. The token that did not move IS the end, and the walk now says so.

2. tests/live_server.py: the /bookmarks-paged route answered from a process-wide counter keyed by route, so the first request got page one and the second got page two whatever they carried. The fixture would have served page two to a run that had dropped the cursor, which is the one bug that route exists to catch, and a second case on the route would have started at page two because the first had run. The answer is now a function of the request's own cursor: no cursor is page one, LIVECURSOR1 is page two, an unknown token is an empty timeline.

Acceptance: all four stop conditions are pinned by unit cases under a --count no page can meet, so the ask is never what ends the walk; the paged stand-in is stateless and order-independent; the e2e transcript is byte-identical, since neither change alters the wire for the case that already ran. Gates: PROOF (ALL PROOFS CHECK), --check-only, the eight suites and tests/e2e.sh all green. Learning recorded in docs/learnings/a-cursor-that-comes-back-unchanged-cannot-advance.md.
